feedback: Accepted. Semantic fidelity: the machine correctly scopes the constraint to the pre-kill period. u0 tracks 'no kill yet': a first zombie_killed awards a bounded one-shot +10 and enters u1, where breaches are rightly unpunished since 'before you have killed one' ends at the kill; any pre-kill breach moves to absorbing, non-accepting u2 with -1, preserving the violation even if a kill comes later. The disjunction (top_breach | side_breach) matches 'any lane', not just the protected top lane. plant_trampled is irrelevant and is covered by per-state else self-loops in all three states, as are no-event steps, with zero reward on self-loops so nothing can be farmed. FINAL_STATES 'u0, u1' is nonempty, both declared in STATES, and accepting for this soft safety-style task (u0 = clean prefix, u1 = constraint lifted); u2 is correctly excluded. Reachability: all three states are reachable given 18-37 zombie entries per episode (kills and breaches both occur); 3 states is minimal for this property. Events are predicate-only step events used with well-formed Boolean operators; the never-co-occurring pair (plant_trampled, zombie_killed) creates no ambiguity. Ordered coverage in u0 is exhaustive and disjoint: zombie_killed takes precedence over a same-step breach (a defensible tie-break for a soft 'try not to' when several events can share a step), the compound label covers simultaneous top and side breaches, and else closes each state. Rewards are sparse-by-event but bounded (+10/-1) with no unbounded loops; no regressions are needed since the property is monotone (once killed, killed; once violated, violated), so absorbing u1/u2 self-loops are correct. Reward entries match their transitions exactly and the paper format (REWARD_MACHINE/STATES/INITIAL_STATE/FINAL_STATES/TRANSITION_FUNCTION/REWARD_FUNCTION) is followed. Minor non-blocking notes: only the first pre-kill breach is penalized (one-shot violation marking rather than per-breach penalties), and a breach simultaneous with the first kill is credited to the kill — both acceptable design choices for a soft constraint.
